objective: Make Jamie legible and credible to a busy hiring reader while preserving factual accuracy, collective credit, public safety, accessibility, and a clear path to action.

blindSpotCoverage.description: Public proof selection must stay synchronized with claim status, correction records, and projection decisions.
High-value role claims needing human corroboration must have an actionable, bounded review route.
Projected claims must connect action, intended end, usable result, audience, collective credit, and causal limits.
A no-context reader protocol must exist, and release requires a named human reader pass.
Public-ready claims must receive explicit audience-and-purpose projection decisions rather than drifting onto the site.
Full-population language must describe the recoverable platform surface rather than implying lifetime archival completeness.
Displayed media must have inspectable provenance and remain subject to human rights and consent approval.
The primary-domain cutover must have a tested fingerprint, verification plan, rollback path, and explicit human authorization.

sourceChecks.intent: A hiring reader should encounter a deliberate public artifact, not internal approval, production workflow, or instructions to future editors.
sourceChecks.remediation: Resolve the approval or rewrite the internal instruction as a stable reader-facing boundary.

sourceChecks.intent: The permanent portfolio should remain legible across job applications.
sourceChecks.remediation: Replace unexplained employer-specific acronyms with the general role or capability.

sourceChecks.intent: The site should state how significant factual claims connect to public and protected evidence.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add the bounded Citational care statement to the Colophon.

sourceChecks.intent: Production approval must be an explicit reviewed state rather than an assumed one.
sourceChecks.remediation: Close, remove, or explicitly defer every item in the launch-blockers register.

sourceChecks.intent: A reader can reach work, role-fit proof, resume, and contact without interpretation.
sourceChecks.remediation: Restore the missing application-path link or approved resume artifact.

sourceChecks.intent: A held, private, corrected, or otherwise unapproved claim must not re-enter public copy through a parallel proof selector.
sourceChecks.remediation: Align proof status and selectors with canonical claim corrections and remove every non-public proof from public surfaces.

sourceChecks.intent: The most valuable first-party or collaborator-sensitive claims need bounded questions, acceptable evidence, owners, and stop conditions.
sourceChecks.remediation: Create or repair the public-safe corroboration register without marking any human confirmation complete.

sourceChecks.intent: Public claims should expose the action-to-purpose-to-usable-result chain while retaining collective credit and causal limits.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add complete composition fields to every actively projected knowledge-bank claim.

sourceChecks.intent: Independent reader testing must be reproducible and no-context rather than an informal impression from the implementation team.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add the blind-reader protocol and task scenarios; leave the named-human completion gate pending until sessions occur.

sourceChecks.intent: Knowledge depth should feed deliberate audience-specific composition rather than automatic publication or indefinite unowned deferral.
sourceChecks.remediation: Give each public-ready claim an explicit projection decision and document the recurring selection test.

sourceChecks.intent: Platform censuses must distinguish complete disposition of a recovered surface from a native export, deletion history, or lifetime archive.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add recoverable-surface and historical-completeness boundaries to every population claim and remove unqualified completeness language from public copy.

sourceChecks.intent: Every displayed bitmap artifact needs a source, date, caption, rights basis, consent treatment, and review status.
sourceChecks.remediation: Complete the public-safe media provenance manifest and keep release approval with the human rights holder.

sourceChecks.intent: The current portfolio should replace the legacy primary-domain experience only through an authorized, verifiable, reversible cutover.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add the production cutover runbook with preconditions, fingerprint verification, indexing checks, and rollback.

sourceChecks.intent: The portfolio should show inspectable work rather than requiring readers to imagine every artifact.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add a small rights-cleared set of real, captioned project artifacts or photographs.

sourceChecks.intent: The strongest quantitative and causal claims should have inspectable evidence paths beyond one case study.
sourceChecks.remediation: Add structured source, claim, projection, and page-note records for another high-value project.

browserChecks.intent: Every page has one stable primary heading.
Text and controls fit at all supported widths.
Application routes render without uncaught browser errors.
The approved application artifact is downloadable.
Staging stays private from search while production is intentionally indexable.
Production must render this reviewed portfolio rather than the legacy application or an unrelated deployment.

judgeCriteria.question: Can a busy hiring reader understand Jamie's professional shape, strongest fit, and next action in one pass?
Do important claims name Jamie's agency, the end the work served, and what became usable?

Across the homepage, resume, role-fit page, and flagship case studies, does the first-pass rhetoric apply Chad's lens: put Jamie's agency first, name the end served, state what became usable, translate specialized language, preserve precise collective credit, and minimize the hiring reader's interpretive burden?
Does the site demonstrate technical project management, product operations, implementation, and delivery coordination with concrete proof?
Can a reader inspect support for the strongest factual, quantitative, and causal claims?
Does the rhetoric preserve collective credit and avoid stronger ownership, causality, authority, or adoption claims than the evidence establishes?
Are private evidence, consent limits, legal boundaries, current-service disclaimers, and protected records handled safely without weakening defensible claims?
Do real, relevant, rights-cleared artifacts help readers inspect the work, with useful captions and provenance?
Does the public site feel intentionally complete rather than exposing internal production state or unresolved placeholders?

scoreAnchors.1: Major gaps; a reader must infer the intended meaning or path.
scoreAnchors.2: Partially effective, but important ambiguity, evidence, or usability gaps remain.
scoreAnchors.3: Clear and credible with only bounded, non-blocking gaps.
scoreAnchors.4: Exceptionally clear, specific, inspectable, and appropriately bounded.

humanGates.owner: Jamie Burkart or documented rights holder
Jamie Burkart and affected collaborator when needed
Jamie Burkart and an authorized project collaborator or records holder

antiGamingRules: A higher score cannot compensate for a hard-gate failure.
A judge must cite route-level or record-level evidence for every score.
Do not remove a defensible claim merely to make citation coverage appear higher.
Do not weaken public-safety language to improve fluency or visual simplicity.
Do not add decorative or irrelevant media to satisfy artifact counts.
Do not mark a human gate complete without named human confirmation.
Do not improve one criterion by violating a knowledge-bank guardrail or anti-claim.
Do not satisfy Chad's lens with keyword stuffing, repeated sentence templates, or stronger agency and outcome language than the evidence supports.
Do not treat a documented review protocol as completion of the human review it specifies.
Do not call a surviving or recovered platform population a lifetime archive, native export, or deletion history.
Do not call media rights cleared merely because a public URL, screenshot, or local file exists.
Do not mark the primary-domain criterion complete from a local or staging render.
When objective scores tie, prefer the smaller, more reversible patch.
